entries.title: I Corinthians 14:1
segments: Prophesy. 'Prophesy' in the Scriptures signifies not merely nor chiefly foretelling the future, but uttering truth under divine inspiration.  Large portions of the books of the Old Testament prophets, as Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, etc., are devoted to the description of present or past events, advice, reproof, and the like.  This sense of the word prophesy is especially prominent in the New Testament (
and note thereon).

entries.title: I Corinthians 14:2
segments: He that speaketh in a tongue, etc. Speaking in a tongue or tongues, a kind of ecstatic utterance, is in 1 and 2 Corinthians different from speaking with 'other tongues,' that is, in foreign languages, as recorded in
.  The utterance of him who spoke in a tongue might be unknown to all the hearers.  See
.  In
the speaking with tongues apparently means speaking in foreign languages; but in 1 and 2 Corinthians the gift is best taken to signify an ecstatic utterance, not intelligible until interpreted.  See

entries.title: I Corinthians 14:4
segments: Edifieth himself. He himself is supposed to understand the words he speaks.

entries.title: I Corinthians 14:6
segments: If I come unto you, speaking with tongues. See

entries.title: I Corinthians 14:11
segments: A barbarian. This had no reference to personal character or grade of civilization.  The Greeks called every one not a Greek a barbarian, that is, one who spoke an unintelligible tongue.

entries.title: I Corinthians 14:12
segments: The edifying of the church. The purpose that should be controlling.  See

entries.title: I Corinthians 14:13
segments: Pray that be may interpret. The two powers of speaking in a tongue and of interpreting the utterance seem not to have been always joined in the same person.

entries.title: I Corinthians 14:18
segments: I speak with tongues more than you all. The only definite statement that Paul possessed the gift of tongues, which he mentions here incidentally.  His use of Greek to the chief captain (
) and of the Aramaic or 'Hebrew' (
) implies nothing miraculous or more than any well educated Jew of that day might have done.

entries.title: I Corinthians 14:23
segments:
Men unlearned or unbelieving.  The meetings were public; unbelievers could freely come.  The Christian assemblies were never secret until persecution made them so.
 

 
 Say that ye are mad.  Such visitors being evidently unable to understand the utterances.

entries.title: I Corinthians 14:24
segments: He is reproved, etc. By the power of spiritual truth spoken in a language with which he is familiar.  See

entries.title: I Corinthians 14:25
segments: Fall down on his face.  With the face near the ground or the floor, the forehead supported on clasped hands; the oriental posture of adoration and supplication.  See

entries.title: I Corinthians 14:26
segments: Each one hath, etc. Abundant resources and readiness; although these might tend to confusion unless discretely ordered.  There was one rule for this: Let all things be done unto edifying.

entries.title: I Corinthians 14:27
segments:
By two, or at the most three. Paul considered the gift of speaking in a tongue a dangerous one, to be guardedly manifested.
 

 
 In turn. One at a time, indicating that two or more may have been previously allowed to speak at once, producing the 'confusion' of

.
 

 
 And let one interpret. 'That the church may receive edifying' (

entries.title: I Corinthians 14:29
segments: Let the prophets speak by two or three. Two or three such exercises on one occasion, following each other in orderly sequence.

entries.title: I Corinthians 14:30
segments: But if a revelation be made, etc. Let any speaker close his remarks if he perceives that another has received a sudden revelation.

entries.title: I Corinthians 14:31
segments: One by one. One at a time; two or three of one kind of exercise to be heard in immediate sequence.

entries.title: I Corinthians 14:32
segments: The spirits of the prophets are subject, etc. Those who exercise the prophetic gift must control it.

entries.title: I Corinthians 14:33
segments:
Confusion. The apostle meant: be sure God cannot work in you in confusion, for that is not His way, and does not fittingly manifest nor can it glorify Him.
 

 
 Peace. Goes fitly with the 'love' of
.  The two terms are often joined.  See

entries.title: I Corinthians 14:34
segments:
, 35
 
 Let the women keep silence, etc. To be read in connection with

.  In those verses praying or prophesying by women under proper conditions seems to be permitted.  The force of the present passage has been much disputed, some expositors and churches holding that the prohibition is for all places and all times; others urging that it was local and temporary, for the places and the period with reference to which the apostle wrote, where the general seclusion of women would cause any public activity to be held 'shameful,' like the dispensing with the veil.

entries.title: I Corinthians 14:39
segments: Let all things be done decently, etc. The object of all the special instructions here given.
